accepted_units.title: A filtration becomes a persistent invariant through compatible induced maps
accepted_units.why_material: The source turns an arbitrary scale choice into a structured family: nested representations induce homology objects and composition-compatible maps, so information is tracked across all scales rather than read from one snapshot. This is a reusable move from parameterized representations to a functorial invariant.
accepted_units.context_note: This is expository synthesis, not a source-original theorem. The persistence-module terminology and its interval consequences are attributed to the established literature; the unit records the semantic mechanism only.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate. The mechanism depends on treating the nested complexes and induced maps as one ordered diagram; exact normalized formulas and field notation should be checked against the PDF before symbolic reuse.

accepted_units.title: Compatible bases compress persistence into intervals, with a boundary on birth-death narratives
accepted_units.why_material: A compatible-basis classification compresses a system of vector spaces and maps into interval lifetimes, but the text also shows that an intuitive elder-rule narrative is not well-defined when classes are born simultaneously. The combination is useful for distinguishing invariant classification from basis-dependent stories about individual generators.
accepted_units.context_note: The Fundamental Theorem of Persistent Homology is cited rather than proved here. The simultaneous-birth caveat is an expository warning and should not be presented as a new classification result.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High. Barcode intervals require a one-parameter total order, field coefficients, and compatible bases; normalized inequality and inverse-image glyphs are imperfect, so exact symbolic definitions need source verification.

accepted_units.title: Choose a combinatorial model by balancing guarantees, computability, and size
accepted_units.why_material: The source makes representation choice explicit: a complex should approximate the intended topology, yet intersection-based constructions may be expensive, while pairwise clique constructions are easier to form but remain large in the worst case and provide only a controlled approximation under stated geometry. This is a generic exactness-versus-tractability comparison.
accepted_units.context_note: The approximation inclusions, complexity bounds, and algorithms are tutorial material attributed to cited sources. Later construction surveys provide supporting alternatives but are not treated as independent theorem evidence here.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High. The comparison changes with ambient geometry, scale convention, truncation dimension, and complex construction; the damaged epsilon and exponent glyphs preclude relying on exact constants from the normalized text.

accepted_units.title: Separate preservation guarantees from heuristic search for a useful reduction
accepted_units.why_material: The reduction step has two logically distinct claims: permitted same-filtration collapses preserve persistent homology, whereas finding an optimal or practically small reduction can be intractable and is therefore heuristic. This cleanly separates semantic correctness of a transformation from an unguaranteed search strategy for efficiency.
accepted_units.context_note: The preservation results, NP-completeness statement, and named reduction methods are all cited background. The source does not prove speedup or optimality for a particular heuristic.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate. Preservation depends on filtration-compatible matchings or the stated collapse class; tidy-set and strong-collapse claims must not be transferred to arbitrary filtrations.

accepted_units.title: A filtration-compatible boundary representation exposes birth-death pairings
accepted_units.why_material: Ordering simplices compatibly with faces and filtration converts the filtered complex into a boundary matrix; reduction then identifies pivot pairings that translate back into finite or infinite persistence intervals. This is a reusable change of representation linking combinatorial inclusion data to a classified summary.
accepted_units.context_note: The algorithm is standard cited material, not a new contribution. The unit captures the correctness interface and pairing semantics, not the subsequent concrete matrix execution or dataset-dependent optimizations.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High. Correct interpretation depends on the filtration-compatible order, field coefficients, column-reduction convention, and exact pivot definition; normalized matrix and inequality glyphs require verification before executable use.

accepted_units.title: Equivalent summaries support comparison only after a metric or feature-space choice
accepted_units.why_material: The source distinguishes two ways to make barcode output comparable: regard equivalent persistence diagrams as points in a metric space and match them, or map diagrams into spaces suited to statistical operations. It then states the stability interface: under suitable hypotheses, perturbations of the filtered input are controlled by bottleneck distance at the output.
accepted_units.context_note: This section is a literature survey. The distances, feature maps, and stability theorem are cited results, and the source does not establish that any one statistical representation is universally preferable.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High. Diagram comparison depends on diagonal multiplicity, the ground metric and Wasserstein parameter; feature mappings can forget information, and the stability claim holds only under unstated favorable conditions in the cited theorem. Formula glyphs should be checked before exact use.

accepted_units.title: Changing the indexing geometry breaks interval classification
accepted_units.why_material: Zigzag diagrams remain computable when arrows reverse, but varying more than one independent parameter removes the one-dimensional interval decomposition on which barcode compression relies. The source thereby identifies indexing order, not merely algorithm choice, as a structural boundary of the representation.
accepted_units.context_note: The zigzag and simplicial-map algorithms and the failure of the one-parameter Fundamental Theorem are cited background. This unit records the stated obstruction without claiming a complete classification of multiparameter persistence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High. The conclusion depends on the diagram category and partial-order geometry; the normalized two-parameter diagram is visually damaged, so only the surrounding prose is reliable evidence.
